title: Wayfinding: Career Map, Role Progression, and Benefits Reference
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This page is a single-reference handbook for new and existing contributors outlining: the role progression model used at Redwood, how to find and request role changes or internal rotations, the benefits and perks map that often inform total rewards conversations, and a compact internal tools checklist that new hires and managers can use to validate access during the first 90 days.

Purpose and audience

- Purpose: Reduce friction for role progression decisions, make the promotion/transfer steps predictable, and centralize benefit entry points so managers and ICs make aligned choices.
- Audience: all Redwood employees, hiring managers, people-ops partners, and engineering leads.

Scope and governance

- Scope: Applies to all full-time employees (FTE), regular contractors on 6+ month programs, and managers approving role changes. Not intended for external consultants or short-term contractors.
- Governance: People Ops maintains policy (owner: @people-ops). Role evaluation panels (REP) are chaired by the Staff+ engineering manager on duty for technical roles and the Senior Product Lead for product roles.

Role architecture: at-a-glance

Redwood uses a leveled ladder with clear competency buckets. Each role family (engineering, platform, product, design, research, support, sales) has a published competency matrix that maps to expectations across: impact, scope, technical craft, leadership, and influence.

Quick reference table (example for Engineering family)

| Level | Title (common) | Expected horizon | Typical scope | Promotion authority |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| IC1 | Associate Engineer | 6–12 months | Owns small components, PR-level work | Team Manager |
| IC2 | Engineer | 12–24 months | Cross-component ownership, shipping features | Manager + Rep panel |
| IC3 | Senior Engineer | 24–48 months | End-to-end product areas, mentoring | Rep panel |
| IC4 | Staff Engineer | 36+ months | Cross-team architecture, technical strategy | REP + Org Head |
| M1–M4 | Engineering Manager → Director | Varies | Team to org leadership | People Ops + Director approvals |
Each family page contains detailed competency checklists. See Related pages for the full matrices.

How to read the ladders

- Competencies are behavioral and deliverable-based — reviewers use evidence (PRs, incident reports, product metrics, customer feedback) rather than subjective impressions.
- Expect a 6–12 week calibration period during transitions when goals and success metrics are re-scoped.

Promotion and internal transfer procedure (step-by-step)

1. Prepare packet (IC or Manager): 1–page case summary, 3–6 evidence items (PR links, launch metrics, peer feedback), and proposed new title/level. Use the Promotion Packet template in Confluence (/confluence/templates/promotion-packet).
2. Manager endorsement: manager adds a written endorsement in the packet and submits to People Ops via the Promotion Intake form (People Ops app in Slack #people-ops).
3. REP review: the Role Evaluation Panel meets weekly; they will accept, request more evidence, or decline. Expect a decision in 7–14 days from submission for standard cases.
4. Calibration & compensation: when level changes affect comp bands, People Ops issues a compensation proposal and a manager schedules a calibration conversation with the candidate.
5. Announcement & documentation: People Ops updates HRIS (Workday) and the public-facing team directory. Manager schedules a transition retro and updates team responsibilities.

Checklist for internal rotation (different team)

- Candidate: writes a 1-page objective and transferable skills list.
- Hiring manager (target team): posts a short role brief and schedules a 30-min intro call.
- Current manager: approves transition timeline and signals open hiring slot/backfill plan.
- People Ops: creates cross-team transfer packet; if promotion is requested, route through REP.

Compensation and benefits primer (concise)

- Compensation bands: Redwood uses banded salary ranges per level and role family. Bands are updated annually; band midpoints align with market percentile targets set by Finance + People Ops.
- Bonus & equity: target-level bonuses tied to level and role (see Compensation Guidelines page). Equity refresh cadence: typical for Staff+ and promotion events.
- Benefits snapshot (high level): medical/dental/vision; 401(k) with company match; flexible parental leave; commuter stipend (where office present); remote work home office stipend; professional development allowance.

Perk highlights and eligibility table

| Perk | Who is eligible | Owner/contact |
|---|---|---|
| Home office stipend (USD up to $1,200) | All FTE | People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com) |
| Learning & development allowance ($2,000/yr) | All FTE | L&D (learning@redwood.com) |
| Parental leave (16 weeks primary) | FTE, after 90 days | People Ops |
| Conference attendance (pre-approval) | Teams with manager approval | Manager + Finance |
| Dedicated wellbeing stipend | FTE | People Ops |
How benefits tie to role changes

- Title/level changes do not retroactively change eligibility effective before the new start date. Some perks (conference budget, L&D) are prorated on the effective date. Finance/People Ops will note pro-ration in the compensation packet.

Onboarding and first-90-days tools checklist

Managers and new hires should verify the following within 30 days and re-check at 90 days. This list emphasizes commonly missed access points.

1. Identity & access
- Okta: MFA enabled and device registered.
- Google Workspace: email group membership for org/team.
- GitHub: repo access for team projects and private model catalog.

2. Developer & infra access
- GCP project access: request via infra-access form.
- Terraform state: read access for non-prod work; write after approval and pair onboarding.
- Buildkite / CI: pipelines and deploy keys added.

3. Product & tracking
- Linear: team board and project access.
- Segment/Rudder or PostHog: product analytics access if the role requires it.

4. Service and runtime access (engineering-specific)
- Redwood Console (internal): token with read-only first, escalate to deploy scope during pair session.
- Staging clusters: read & logs; prod access requires on-call completion and manager sign-off.

Mini-table: Access levels and typical owners

| Tool | Typical initial access | Who to contact |
|---|---|---|
| Okta | Provisioned by People Ops | people-ops@redwood.com |
| GitHub | Team repo access | Eng team lead |
| GCP | Non-prod projects | infra-access@redwood.com |
| Redwood Console | Read-only token | runtime-ops@redwood.com |

Onboarding CLI & config snippet examples

- To configure your local git:
  git config --global user.email "first.last@redwood.com"
  git config --global user.name "First Last"

- Example: set up readline for Redwood Console CLI (internal package)
  # install (mac/linux)
  curl -sSL https://internal.redwood.com/cli/install.sh | bash
  rw-cli login --sso --org redwood-internal

Manager responsibilities in first 90 days

- Prepare a 30/60/90 plan with explicit outcomes. Add measurable signals of success (metrics, PR cadence, bug reduction, customer feedback).
- Schedule weekly 1:1s (minimum) and a 30-day check-in with People Ops.
- Conduct skip-level introductions within 45 days.
- Ensure training budget and onboarding pair sessions are scheduled.

Case examples and defaults

- Fast-track technical promotion: used when an IC demonstrates clear cross-team technical leadership AND has shipped a measurable product improvement or cost saving. Expect expedited REP review (decision in 7 calendar days).
- Cross-functional lateral transfer: typically a 2–6 week handoff with overlapping pairing; hiring manager and current manager jointly set the backlog for the overlap window.

Escalation and disputes

- If a candidate disagrees with REP outcome, they may request a calibration review within 10 business days. People Ops will convene a separate calibration panel (Org Head + People Ops + neutral senior peer).
- Compensation disputes escalate to People Ops and Finance for final determination.

Templates and links (quick access)

- Promotion packet template: /confluence/templates/promotion-packet
- Internal rotation brief template: /confluence/templates/rotation-brief
- Onboarding access form (Okta/GCP/GitHub): /confluence/internal-forms/access-request
- Compensation guidelines: /confluence/finance/compensation-guidelines-2026

Frequently asked questions (short)

Q: How long from submission to promotion effective date?
A: Standard cases: 2–6 weeks; fast-track: 1 week. Effective date is typically the start of the next payroll period after approval.

Q: Can I request a promotion during an internal rotation?
A: Yes. Include both objectives in the promotion packet and indicate the proposed effective org. The REP will consider cross-team impact.

If you believe there are missing items or edge cases (international hires, special equity cases), please open a request in the People Ops backlog or email people-ops@redwood.com.
